nodes.name: Pt(111)/H2O interface construction
nodes.procedure: Construction of 4-layer (5×5) unit cell of Pt(111) surface slab. The interface model contains a water bilayer over a monolayer of adsorbed hydrogen. A vacuum region of 15 Å thickness is further added above the water layers in order to decouple periodic images of the slab model. Periodic boundary condition (PBC) for modeling the Pt/H2O interface supercell with size of 14.06 Å × 14.06 Å × 30.89 Å. The k-point mesh for sampling the Brillouin zone of the slab model is set as 2×2×1. The kinetic energy cutoff is set to 100 Ry (1360 eV). Compensating charge plate in the vacuum region right above the water solvation layer (~2 Å) to maintain the overall charge neutrality of the supercell.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations performed on the 4-layer (5×5) Pt(111) surface slab model with water bilayer and adsorbed hydrogen monolayer, using ABACUS software with NAO basis set.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The first-principles calculation software ABACUS is employed to perform all DFT calculations. A notable feature of ABACUS is its use of numerical atomic orbitals (NAOs) as the basis set...

nodes.characterization_summary: Machine learning force field (DP-Ne MLP) trained using DP-GEN workflow with RMSE of energies 0.6 meV/atom and forces 54 meV/Å on 200-snapshot test set from Pt(111)/H2O interface trajectories, enabling accurate grand canonical simulations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3, a good agreement is achieved on the testing data set. The total root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of energies and forces on the testing data set are 0.6 meV/atom and 54 meV/Å, respectively.
